title: 2011 AMC 12B Problem 13
statement: Brian writes down four integers \(w \gt x \gt y \gt z\) whose sum is \(44.\) The pairwise positive differences of these numbers are \(1,\) \(3,\) \(4,\) \(5,\) \(6,\) and \(9.\) What is the sum of the possible values for \(w?\)

solutions.text:
The largest difference is \(w-z=9.\) For either interior number \(n,\) we have \(9=(w-n)+(n-z).\) The only pairs among the listed differences that sum to \(9\) are \(3+6\) and \(4+5,\) so the remaining difference must be \(x-y=1.\)

The second largest difference \(6\) is either \(w-y\) or \(x-z.\) If \(w-y=6,\) the numbers are \(\{w,w-5,w-6,w-9\},\) so \(4w-20=44\) and \(w=16.\) If \(x-z=6,\) the numbers are \(\{w,w-3,w-4,w-9\},\) so \(4w-16=44\) and \(w=15.\)

The possible values are \(16\) and \(15,\) which sum to \(31.\)

Thus, the correct answer is B.
hints: The largest difference is \(w-z=9,\) and the smallest positive difference must be \(x-y=1\)
The second largest difference \(6\) is either \(w-y\) or \(x-z\); handle each case
